BiblicalUsage: A herdsman is the word for a cattle-tender, and it appears once, in Amos's defence of his calling. In Amos 7:14 Amos says, I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet's son, but I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit — and then the Lord took him as he followed the flock and said, go, prophesy unto my people Israel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Amos's herdsman is the pattern of God's prophets: not a prophet's son, but a man taken from the flock to speak to the nation.
